verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
verse.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
verse.translation: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is hesitating, wondering if he should abandon his duty as a warrior because it is bloody and painful. Krishna tells him that no work is perfect. Every path has flaws, just as fire always has smoke. The work that fits your own nature is still your work, even with its smoke. You do not throw it away because of the smoke. You do it as an offering, flaws and all.
verse.for_you: The fire you feel is your own, not borrowed from a salary or a title. The work you chose to build has its own smoke. Keep doing it as an offering. Let the flaws be part of the work, not a reason to walk away.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: पुरुषार्थात्फलप्राप्तिर्देशकालवशादिह । प्राप्ता चिरेण शीघ्रं वा यासौ दैवमिति स्मृता ॥
verse.line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.
verse.translation: Results come from effort, sooner or later, depending on place and time. That arrival of the fruit, early or late, is what people call fate.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is teaching the young Rama that what people call fate is only the fruit of effort, delayed by time and place. He tells Rama that his past actions shaped his present, and his present actions will shape his future. The timing of results is not magic. It is simply the natural arrival of what you have already planted through your own work.
verse.for_you: You quit your job and the fire is real. But the mind will start watching for the prize instead of the work. Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate. Your past effort shaped this morning. Today's effort shapes tomorrow.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari tells the reader to let the world praise or blame, let money come or go, and let death come today or ages hence. The steadfast do not step off the right path. He says setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path, because a struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
verse.for_you: You are building your brand right now, and that path is already right. Let the praise and the doubt come and go. The hard weeks are just noise around a path that is already yours.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.meaning: Vidura speaks to King Dhritarashtra in the dark of the night, before the great peace talks. He tells him that a person is called wise when they decide calmly, begin the work, and do not stop halfway, waste time, or lose their grip on themselves. The work is to decide, and then to begin. To keep going steadily is the measure of a wise person.
verse.for_you: You have already decided to leave the job and build this brand. Now you could keep your hand steady on the wheel, especially when the work feels like a grind. Do one small thing today that moves the brand forward, and let the results be what they are.

story.title: Parvati holds to her choice
story.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
story.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
story.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

script: You are running on a fire you lit yourself. The fear is not about money. It is the fear that this fire will go out before it becomes something real.

Arjuna is on the battlefield. He is looking at the faces of the men he must fight. He is hesitating, wondering if he should abandon his work as a warrior because it is bloody and painful. And Krishna replies:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्, सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः.
In plain words: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.

Krishna says that every path has flaws. All work has some smoke, just as fire always has smoke. You do not throw the work away because of the smoke. You do the work that fits your nature, flaws and all. This is the truth underneath. It is not about staying in a bad situation. It is about letting the work you chose have its imperfections.

For you, today. The fire you feel is your own, not borrowed from a salary or a title. The work you chose to build has its own smoke. Keep doing it as an offering. Let the flaws be part of the work, not a reason to walk away.
What will you do with the smoke?
